physicalNotes: Radius: Rp/R* 0.09783 (the Eigenspectra fitting script's rprs, Figure1.py in Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14751570; Coulombe et al. 2023, Nature 620, 292, Table 3: 0.09783 +/- 0.00028 from TESS) times the host record's radius. The Challener, Weiner Mansfield et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy (arXiv:2510.24708), deposited ThERESA configuration wasp-18b-3d-8bin-sinusoidal-tiovo.cfg in Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14751570 gives the same 0.13177701 solar radii. A sphere: tidal and rotational flattening are not modelled. GM from that file's planet mass, 0.009956036 solar masses (10.4 Jupiter masses), times the JPL solar GM.

sources.period: Eigenspectra fitting script (Figure1.py, planetparams['per']) in Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14751570: 0.941452382 d, as Coulombe et al. (2023), Table 3 (0.941452382 +/- 0.000000069 d)
sources.shape: Eigenspectra fitting script (Figure1.py): ars 3.48023 and inc 84.35320 degrees, the 'final fit' of the deposited light curves; eccentricity 0, as the maps were fitted. The deposited ThERESA configuration gives the same a/R* and 84.38 degrees; Coulombe et al. (2023), Table 3 gives 3.496 and 84.09 from TESS.
sources.phase: Eigenspectra fitting script (Figure1.py): t0 2459802.4078798565 BJD_TDB = 59801.9078798565 BMJD_TDB, the transit before the JWST eclipse of 2022-08-24 (t_sec 2459802.8786060475)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north), as in the ThERESA configuration (Omega 0).
